Issued at 208 PM CDT Sun Oct 25 2026

Monday - Tuesday: Cooler Monday with Some Rain Chances

Monday will feature the coolest temperatures over the next week in 
light of a cold front that had passed through the region with 
northeasterly to easterly surface flow and zonal flow aloft. 
Consequently, high temperatures will fall into the 50s to lower 60s 
across the region. It is important to note though that the average 
high at La Crosse, WI at this point in the year is in the mid-50s so 
we will still be near to slightly above normal on Monday. However, 
as we head into Tuesday, shortwave upper-level ridging and southerly 
surface return flow will instigate a warmer trend for the week with 
highs returning above normal with median high temperatures in the 
NBM in the middle to upper 60s.

As far as precipitation chances are concerned, an approaching 
shortwave impulse moving through the Great Plains will push 
northwest of the local area bringing some resulting rain chances, 
primarily north of I-90 in north-central WI and southeast MN. 
Currently, the latest HREF has fairly respectable probabilities (60-
90%) for measurable precipitation across southeast MN and into north-
central WI. However, given that the bulk of the more robust forcing 
will generally remain to the northwest, more substantial rainfall 
amounts over 0.1" are less likely (20-50%), so not expecting any 
impacts from this rainfall. 

Wednesday - Friday: Unseasonably Warm with Additional Rain Potential 

As we head into the latter half of the work week, continued robust 
southerly flow into Wednesday will allow for increasing 
probabilities (50-90% in the NBM) for highs to top 70 degrees for 
much of the local area. As a result, could see some near record
high temperatures at La Crosse, WI and Rochester, MN with their
record highs being 75 and 73 degrees respectively for October
28th. While Wednesday currently appears to be the warmest day 
reflected in guidance, this unseasonably warm trend likely 
persists through Friday with continued zonal to southwesterly 
synoptic flow in place. 

On the heels of the first shortwave trough on Monday/Tuesday, a 
secondary shortwave pulse tracks northwest of the local area with an 
attending surface front passing through the region Wednesday evening 
and overnight. Consequently, precipitation chances increase (70-90%) 
in the grand ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian) during this timeframe. With 
some elevated instability present in NAM/GFS soundings Wednesday 
evening and overnight, would expect some thunderstorm potential 
which may locally allow for some healthier rainfall amounts. This is 
reflected in the grand ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) which 
has some probabilities (10-40%) for rainfall amounts over 0.25". 
Additional precipitation potential is present for Friday as 
suggested in the NBM, however confidence is somewhat lower at this 
juncture due to some uncertainties on position and timing of various 
synoptic features such as a shortwave impulse pushing towards 
the region in this timeframe and where surface high pressure 
will be located which deterministic guidance disagrees on. 

Saturday - Sunday: Staying Warmer than Normal with Rain Chances

This weekend will continue to feature warmer than normal 
temperatures with upper-level ridging and southerly surface flow in 
place for Saturday. As mentioned previously, the shortwave impulse 
late week and into the weekend has some lingering uncertainty on 
position/timing. That being said, the grand ensemble 
(GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) has very high probabilities (80-90%) for 
measurable precipitation areawide on Saturday. So while the finer 
details are low predictability at this point, thinking that some 
rainfall seems feasible for Halloween, really just a question on 
timing and exact amounts.
